The typed question is lost on failure.

terms.meaning: a shared place where the app keeps data that many screens read and update
a handle that lets code control a visual element directly, such as scrolling it
a small tappable label that offers a ready-made follow-up question
a yes or no value that says whether a request is still in progress

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the chat screen
sections.what: Loads the parts needed for the chat: text input, lists, buttons, the loading spinner, theme colors, a shared card component and the chat store.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. These are needed to draw the chat and read its data.

sections.name: ChatScreen (part 1)
sections.title: Chat state, sending and auto scroll
sections.what: Holds the text being typed and reads the chat data from the store. When the user taps send, it passes the text on and clears the box. After each change to the messages, it scrolls to the newest one. It also draws the header with a new chat button and a welcome message when the chat is empty.
sections.why: Likely reason: the short delay before scrolling gives the list time to draw the new message first. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The typed text is cleared before the send finishes. If sending fails, the user's question is gone and not restored.

sections.name: ChatScreen (part 2)
sections.title: Message list, suggestions and input box
sections.what: Draws every message and a Maate is thinking note while waiting. It shows suggestion chips only when the assistant is not busy. The input box has a send button that is disabled when the box is empty or a reply is loading.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Disabling send while loading stops repeated questions from being sent at once.
sections.watch_out: Tapping a suggestion sends it straight to the store, skipping the empty-text check that the send button uses.

sections.name: MessageBubble
sections.title: Single message bubble
sections.what: Draws one message. User messages sit on the right in purple. Assistant messages sit on the left with a small sparkle icon and can show up to two suggestion chips.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the layout. Splitting sides makes the conversation easy to follow.
sections.watch_out: The role check compares against an uppercase word. If the server sends another case, every message shows on the assistant side. Inside the chip loop, a parameter named s hides the stylesheet also called s. It works, but it is easy to misread when editing.

sections.name: Chip
sections.title: Small local label chip
sections.what: A small bordered label used for suggestion chips inside assistant messages.
sections.why: Likely reason: the comment says this is meant to come from the shared UI kit, so this local copy may be a stand-in. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: This is a separate copy, not the shared chip. Design changes to the shared version will not reach this screen.

summary: The Maate AI chat screen, where the user types health questions, reads replies, and taps suggested follow-up questions.
purpose: Lets the user ask questions about their own health records and read the assistant's answers in a conversation view.
why: Reason not stated beyond the welcome text, which says the assistant answers questions about reports, medications and medical history.
how: The screen reads messages, the loading state and suggestions from the chat store. When the user taps send, the text goes to the store and the box is cleared. The message list scrolls to the newest message. Each message is drawn as a bubble, and assistant replies can show up to two suggestion chips.
inputs: Typed text, taps on send and on suggestion chips, and the messages, loading flag and suggestions from the chat store.
outputs: A visible chat transcript, a loading note while waiting, and tappable follow-up suggestions. The screen does not save anything itself.
risks: The typed text is cleared before the send is confirmed, so a failed send loses the question. The role check is case sensitive, so an unexpected case from the server shows messages on the wrong side.
debug: If messages appear on the wrong side, check the role value the store provides. If nothing is sent, check the store's sendMessage action and the loading flag. If the list does not scroll, check the scroll timer and the messages dependency.
